Hi all — quick note with the core points I'll include in the narrative (draft below). I attached the first-pass PNG and a compact checklist PDF (controlplane-egress-checklist.pdf).

Draft narrative (one-paragraph + bullets):
Redwood's envelope model creates a hardened trust boundary between edge inference surfaces and the customer-dedicated control plane used in Private/Dedicated deployments. At deployment time a per-tenant envelope is instantiated that enforces: network separation (VPC isolation + enforced egress ACLs), crypto separation (per-tenant KMS keys managed via customer or Redwood KMS integrations), and runtime tenancy fences (process-level isolation and per-request tracing). Operational attestations are emitted at the envelope boundary (TLS client certs, signed enrollment tokens) and stored with immutable audit logs to support SOC 2/AICPA controls.

Key attestation points to highlight for reviewers:
- Enrollment: edge nodes present a signed enrollment token issued by Redwood's provisioning CA.
- Control-plane access: control-plane operations only use short-lived mTLS creds scoped to the tenant envelope.
- Egress policy: all egress from the envelope is through a constrained NAT with allow-lists and HTTP header scrubbing; flows to external telemetry are mediated by a proxy that strips customer secrets.
- KMS separation: customer keys are either wrapped by customer-managed KMS or by per-tenant keys in Redwood's KMS with strict access policies and audit trails.

Attachments included: envelope_topology_v1.png (annotated), controlplane-egress-checklist.pdf (artifact checklist).

I'll join the 30-min deep dive at 13:00 PST tomorrow.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Security Architect, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: envelope_topology_v1.png; controlplane-egress-checklist.pdf)

3) Is the annotated PNG sufficient evidence for SIG network diagrams or do you prefer we include a separate CAIQ attachment with specific control mappings?

If you can add the anonymized token sample and the HSM confirmation to the checklist by Monday morning (2027-04-19 09:00 PST), we can close the SOC 2 pre-review.
